mem.10:
23 Jan 2023 — Session 1
- Jolene had a busy week and finished an electrical-engineering project the week before.
- Deborah visited her late mother’s home; her mother died a few years earlier. Jolene’s mother died in 2022. Deborah shared their last photo: two women in wheelchairs hugging. Jolene remembered a bench by the window in her mother’s house. Deborah’s mother loved sitting there each morning; Deborah sometimes sits there to feel close to her.
- Jolene’s mother gave her a heart-shaped bird pendant in Paris in 2010, symbolizing freedom and pursuing goals. Deborah also wears a pendant to remember her mother.
- Deborah hopes to keep teaching yoga and supporting her community; yoga helped her through a difficult time and inspired her to share peace and joy.

27 Jan 2023 — Session 2
- Deborah’s father died suddenly on 25 Jan. Her family was shell-shocked; time together, memories, and looking through family albums/photos gave her peace during difficult times. She shared a photo of her parents’ 1993 wedding. She and her husband value love, openness, and mutual support; she hopes to build a family like her parents’.
- Deborah’s yoga group gave her a thank-you note on 26 Jan. She does yoga in her old home’s living room and still visits because of her mother, who loved reading and travel and read nightly at her favorite window seat. Deborah shared an airplane-window sky photo.
- Jolene’s snakes Susie and Seraphim comfort her. Seraphim once escaped while Jolene gamed, then coiled beside her; photo showed it peeking out of a blanket.
- Jolene said she bought “it” in Paris a year earlier (referent unclear). She and her partner enjoy console games, including *Detroit*; Jolene taught herself gaming as a child. They planned to play *The Walking Dead* on 28 Jan.

1 Feb 2023 — Session 3
- Jolene was excited and nervous about a challenging creative robotics project from her engineering professor; shared robot/laptop photo. She and her partner planned to play a console game together.
- Deborah met neighbor Anna at yoga in the park on 31 Jan. Shared a yellow sign with a family picture; they discussed yoga and community.
- Jolene shared a purse-and-plant photo; when asked about returning to yoga, mentioned planned gaming with her partner.

4 Feb 2023 — Session 4
- Jolene had recently been on an emotional rollercoaster but was coping. She designed and built a sustainable water purifier for a rural community in need. Seeing it work and provide clean water felt surreal and deeply satisfying, gave her purpose, and reminded her engineering can improve lives. She wants to engineer sustainable solutions for underserved communities; Deborah’s support motivated her.
- Deborah and Anna bonded through yoga; shared photo of two women doing a dance pose. They tried poses including Warrior II. Deborah taught a seated chair twist: sit at chair edge, feet planted, twist torso, support with hand on knee, hold briefly, switch; stretches back/shoulders and relieves tension.
- Jolene read *Sapiens*; two weeks earlier she read Neal Stephenson’s *Avalanche* in one sitting. Stories of overcoming challenges reinforced her belief in hard work.
- Deborah recalled someone’s grace and strength through hardship. Flowers from a friend during a difficult time brought hope and comfort; shared bouquet.
- Deborah likes a park with forest trail and nearby beach. Jolene shared Bogotá vacation photos from summer 2022: person with surfboard on beach and sunset over water; it calmed her.
- Deborah finds peace near water by her mother’s old home; shared small-island/lone-boat photo. She brings her mother’s amulet for closeness. Shared woman in white wearing gold-chain necklace; Anna also wears a pendant for her mother.

9 Feb 2023 — Session 5
- Jolene did a “dope” mini-retreat the previous Wednesday (likely 1 Feb) to assess her life; gained perspective and confidence in her achievements.
- Progressing in engineering; interested in green technology for disadvantaged areas. Proposed volunteer program: engineers teach STEM to underprivileged children through workshops at schools/centers and career speakers. Had not contacted organizations, wanting to firm up plan. Shared planner notes; Deborah encouraged her and offered tips/updates.

22 Feb 2023 — Session 6
- Jolene had dinner/drinks with friends on 21 Feb; shared food-and-wine photo.
- Deborah spent time in a nostalgic garden after friend Karlie died the previous week (approx. 15–21 Feb). Roses and dahlias bring peace. Shared last photo with Karlie from summer 2022 hiking; described as two women on a motorcycle on a dirt road. Memories helped her grieve.
- Bali, visited in 2022, is a favorite place: beautiful, peaceful, good for yoga. Shared beach swing photo. Jolene wants to try beach yoga; Deborah praised waves and fresh air; Jolene would keep her posted.

25 Feb 2023 — Session 7
- Jolene balances engineering school and partner’s video games, but uses yoga/meditation to relax, gain perspective, feel alert/motivated, and manage stress. Takes breathing/meditation breaks when overwhelmed; shared woman doing yoga.
- Partner sometimes joins yoga; bonds them. Together three years, unmarried, taking it slowly. Shared hands-with-rings photo; his ring is decorative, not wedding ring.
- Met in college engineering class, became friends then partners. Enjoy collaborating on engineering projects and understand each other’s challenges; shared book/calculator and men outside building.
- Deborah shared sunset-bench photo. Her routine: morning meditation, yoga, teaching; first morning jog at nearby park on 24 Feb, planned to make it routine. Evenings with loved ones. Exercise connects her to her body; self-care enables caring for others (“can’t pour from an empty cup”).

2 Mar 2023 — Session 8
- Deborah enjoyed vegan tofu-vegetable stir-fry with ginger/soy sauce, brought by Anna. Jolene’s comfort food is lasagna; exams kept her busy.
- Jolene squeezed in yoga/meditation on 24 Feb; shared room with wooden floor/window, plus purse/plant photo. Deborah did yoga/meditation to reset.
- Jolene took Seraphim to park on 26 Feb; snake enjoyed it. Shared snake-on-leaves photo; people are surprised it is tame. Deborah likes birdsong/breeze outdoors.
- Jolene felt overwhelmed by exams/deadlines and wanted to monitor stress/mental health; shared desk, notebook, monitor, long to-do list. Deborah advised breaking work into small pieces, setting goals, planners/schedulers, preserving personal time, and offered study-plan help. Encouraging mug photo cheered Jolene up.

13 Mar 2023 — Session 9
- Deborah started neighborhood yoga class; hosted interested neighbors on 10 Mar and shared group photo. Teaching brings calm, happiness, friendships, community, and lets her share peace/awareness. Jolene praised her.
- Jolene struggled with engineering assignments and asked to discuss time management. Deborah agreed to find a mutually convenient time; Jolene would check schedule and get back to her.

22 Mar 2023 — Session 10
- Jolene said exams/deadlines and catching up were stressful. Uses Pomodoro (25 minutes work, 5-minute break), but struggles to prioritize. Deborah shared her daily to-do-list notepad; Jolene shared a notepad of tasks from the previous Friday and said a large stack feels overwhelming and hard to start.
- Deborah introduced the Eisenhower Matrix (sort tasks by urgency/importance), with a photo of scissors on paper. Jolene found the visualization helpful and agreed to try it.
- Deborah encouraged self-care and shared that she and Anna had watched a sunset by the sea and realized they inspire each other. Beach photo showed a person walking with surfboard. Jolene thought of learning to surf but needs spare time. She’s gathering information, watching videos, and bought a beginner’s guide; needs to find time/place for a lesson. Deborah encouraged her; surfboards leaning against palm tree photo inspired Jolene to pursue it. Deborah said the experience matters as much as the outcome,

Jolene’s mother gave her a heart-shaped bird pendant in Paris in 2010, symbolizing freedom and pursuing goals. Yoga helped Deborah through hardship; she hopes to keep teaching and supporting her community.

25–27 Jan — Deborah’s father died suddenly; family was shell-shocked. Family, memories and albums helped. She shared her parents’ 1993 wedding photo and hopes to build a family like theirs, valuing love, openness and support. Yoga group gave her a thank-you note on 26 Jan. Jolene’s snakes Susie and Seraphim comfort her; Seraphim once escaped while she gamed, then curled beside her. Jolene and partner enjoy console games including *Detroit* and *The Walking Dead*.

1–9 Feb — Jolene was excited/nervous about a creative robotics project for her engineering professor: sustainable water purifier for rural community; wants to help underserved communities. Deborah’s support helped her cope. Deborah teaches yoga to help people find balance and reconnect with themselves. On 3 Feb, she and neighbor Anna tried dance poses including Warrior II; supporting each other brought them closer. Jolene read *Sapiens* and Neal Stephenson’s *Avalanche* in one sitting. Deborah finds peace at forest-trail park, beach, and water near her mother’s former house. Jolene shared Bogotá vacation photos from summer 2022 (surfboard, sunset). During a mini-retreat (likely 1 Feb), Jolene gained perspective/confidence and project solutions; proposed volunteer engineers teach STEM to underprivileged children, but hadn’t contacted organizations.

Feb–Mar — Jolene balances engineering school and gaming with partner; yoga, meditation and breathing breaks help her focus/manage stress; partner sometimes joins. Together three years, unmarried and taking it slowly; met in college engineering class, friends first, enjoy collaborating. Hands/rings photo showed his decorative ring, not wedding ring. Deborah’s routine: morning meditation, yoga/teaching, evenings with loved ones; first jog at nearby park 24 Feb. Exercise connects her to body: “can’t pour from an empty cup.” Anna cooked vegan tofu/vegetable stir-fry with ginger/soy; Jolene’s comfort food is lasagna. Exams/deadlines overwhelmed Jolene; Deborah advised small steps, planners, personal time and offered study-plan help. Jolene uses Pomodoro (25 min work/5 min break); Deborah shared to-do pad and Eisenhower matrix. Jolene took Seraphim to park 26 Feb; people surprised snake was tame. Deborah likes birdsong and breeze. Deborah hosted neighbors for yoga 10 Mar; teaching brings calm, happiness, friendship/community. She and Anna watched sunset by sea and realized they inspire each other. Jolene considered surfing and bought beginner guide; project breakthrough 24 Mar. Deborah bought rosemary candle; Jolene likes lavender/rosemary, serene spaces, Nils Frahm and Ólafur Arnalds. Deborah likes mellow instrumentals and “Savana,” recommended *Sleep* for meditation.

Apr–Jun — Deborah biked nearby with neighbor. Art shows evoke her late mother’s love of art/travel, painful but comforting. Jolene says snakes teach her to slow down; gaming with partner relaxes them and brings them closer. In May she completed challenging solar-powered vehicle project (panel on back), a major milestone, then interned at well-known engineering firm; colleagues’ passion renewed ambition. Work-life balance hard. Deborah prepared yoga retreat with friends; shared group yoga in park and beach Dancer Pose photo. Jolene hectic with internship. Bought Seraphim a new aquarium 24 Jun.

Jul–1 Aug — Deborah started running group with Anna and organizes mindfulness/self-care workshops. Jolene fits workouts around study; partner helps her focus when gaming. They like challenges and *It Takes Two*. Jolene shared snake photos; reptile care calms/connects her with nature. Once searched hours for escaped snake, found it under bed, felt love/gratitude. Deborah dislikes dogs, has cats. On 1 Aug she started community cleanup/fundraising project, pleased people came together. Jolene’s major project setback the prior week lost all her work; she felt frustrated/depressed.

12 Aug — Deborah made meditation guide for yoga retreat. Meditation helped Jolene stay calm and regain clarity after lost files. Deborah encouraged deep breaths, remembering her purpose/strengths, self-care and staying in touch. Jolene shared two blue notebooks with galaxy/circuitry design; art gives fresh perspective. She’s developing affordable, productive aerial-surveillance prototype for emergency response/environmental monitoring.

16 Aug — Jolene checked in with boyfriend; relationship felt up and down as she juggled engineering, relationship and growth. Started bullet journal; crossing off tasks feels satisfying; motivational quote reminds her to persist. Deborah advised balance and self-time. Deborah led sunset meditation-yoga for elderly people at local care home the prior week; mindfulness began through workshops/books and is important to her. Jolene keen to try mindfulness; Deborah offered help.

19 Aug — Deborah told Anna her life story the previous Friday; Anna was kind and it felt meaningful. Jolene’s engineering studies going well; balance key. On 17 Aug she bought partner an Xbox; he managed to play it. Deborah’s yoga event the previous month had yoga, food stalls and live music; she contacted businesses/venues. She recommends prioritizing and scheduling study/hobbies. Jolene planned to do so.

21 Aug — Jolene said they’d received *Battlefield 1* for the console the prior week. Deborah visited a memory-filled place and sat on a bench where she and her mother used to talk; felt nostalgia, longing and gratitude. She brought flowers; her mother loved them and simple things. Deborah shared flower photos, including a woman holding red roses. She learned from her mother to slow down, notice beauty and find joy. They discussed appreciating small moments amid busy lives. Jolene is doing more yoga/meditation to relax and focus. Deborah finds balance in yoga, meditation, walks and mindfulness; shared sunset-over-water photo and said walks are a “reboot.” Jolene shared green cushion by window. Her favorite resting yoga pose is savasana/corpse pose; shared humorous photo of person lying on floor with paper bag. She has done yoga for three years, using it to escape study/work stress, and said she was “finding my zen again.” Deborah encouraged her; Jolene thanked her for support.

A past hike with partner to a waterfall oasis made worries disappear; she plans another nature trip next month. Deborah shared a photo of a pink blossom tree near home, magical each spring; it inspired awe and hope for growth through hard times. Jolene shared a plant growing from a building corner as a symbol of resilience and continuing to grow through obstacles; small positive things help her through tough times.
